---
title: "Mind on Start + Void"
description: "Cutover packet for the native Mind Worker: names, bindings, build, smoke checks and rollback."
updatedAt: "2026-11-17"
audience: developers
---

`apps/mind` has native TanStack Start + Vite+ + Void source beside its Next build,
generated by the [start-bridge codemod](/build/devops/start-bridge-codemod). The Next
build and `vercel.json` are untouched, so the current deployment keeps serving until
the route is flipped. `vercel-production-mind.yaml` still deploys the Next app.

## Worker

- Profiles: `VITE_MIND_NATIVE_PROFILE` selects the Worker in `apps/mind/cloudflare/deployment-profile.ts`. Staging (default) is the staging Worker name with `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`; production is `tuturuuu-mind` with `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=0`. Both keep `workers_dev` and `preview_urls` off, and nothing here attaches a route. The qualification job builds and seals both profiles.
- Service bindings: `WORKER_SELF_REFERENCE` targets the profile's own Worker, so a staging artifact binds no production Mind Worker. `ABUSE_GUARD` targets `tuturuuu-abuse-guard` in both profiles because no staging guard Worker exists; the seal allows that one shared target in a staging artifact and rejects any other.
- Publication: `mind` is a protected app in `productionPublicationPolicy` (`tuturuuu.ci.ts`) and `vercel-production-mind.yaml` runs the shared `production-policy` gate before its deploy job. No workflow publishes the Cloudflare Worker.
- Entry: `apps/mind/cloudflare/worker.ts`; Wrangler config is emitted by `void` into `dist`.
- Host: `mind.tuturuuu.com` for the staging profile. Root-only: `mountHosts` is empty and `unknownHost` is `reject`, so `tuturuuu.com/mind` and any other host answer 404 before app code runs.
- Legacy host: in the production profile, `mind.tuturuuu.com` only redirects (`apps/mind/src/runtime/legacy-host.ts`). Every method gets a `307` to `https://tuturuuu.com/mind<path><query>` with `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and no Set-Cookie, after the secret and abuse-guard checks and before any auth, locale or app handling. The origin and base are fixed constants, never read from the Host, a forwarded header, the path or the query; leading slashes and backslashes collapse to one, a path already under `/mind` keeps its prefix, and the query is copied byte for byte. Only `GET`/`HEAD /api/build-info` keeps serving the build identity. Mind ships no service worker, so there is no service-worker exception. Attach the production Worker to `mind.tuturuuu.com` only after the gateway serves `/mind`, or the redirect lands on a 404.
- Mount: the production profile is built for `https://tuturuuu.com/mind` (`basePath` `/mind`, `mountHosts` `tuturuuu.com`; the profile is a build-time literal, not a runtime variable). Mounted browser requests use the strict `supabase-only` session mode from `@tuturuuu/auth/proxy`: only the shared Supabase session on the exact apex origin and base is accepted, app-session cookies, Authorization and the signed-refresh fallback are ignored, and users with an enrolled TOTP factor fail closed. TOTP enrollment is read only from the user that the account assurance check revalidated on the same request; when that user is missing, the mount refuses with `Account assurance unavailable` and never asks the provider factor listing. A cookie-less Authorization is admitted only as a verified coordination token without an app-session or refresh scope, which keeps its existing endpoint verification; any other cookie-less Authorization (a provider JWT, Basic credentials, a browser app-session token) gets `401`. Mounted refusals use `mountedSessionFailureResponse` (`@tuturuuu/auth/proxy/mounted-failure`), which never clears or expires a cookie and carries only the cookie writes of a provider refresh. Every mounted response, including the login and locale redirects (`307`), is `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. The start-bridge handler keeps refusing mounted session minting and strips mounted session writes, so Web stays the only writer of `sb-*` cookies. Locale uses a `mind_locale` cookie at `Path=/mind`. Serving the mount needs the gateway's `MOUNT_MIND` binding with `/mind,/mind/*` in `GATEWAY_MOUNTED_PATHS` ([gateway mounts](/build/devops/gateway-worker)); both stay unset until the cutover is approved.
- Binding: `ASSETS` (static output, `run_worker_first`).
- Variables (names): `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX`, optional `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN` (default `https://tuturuuu.com`).
- Secrets (names, set in the Worker, never in the repo): `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, and `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`. Configure service binding `ABUSE_GUARD` to `tuturuuu-abuse-guard`, secret `ABUSE_GUARD_KEY_PEPPER`, and text variable `ABUSE_GUARD_FAMILIES=proxy`; `ABUSE_GUARD_TIMEOUT_MS` is optional. Upstash is not required. The abuse guard is optional, as on Vercel: with none of `ABUSE_GUARD_KEY_PEPPER`, `ABUSE_GUARD_FAMILIES`, `ABUSE_GUARD_BACKEND` and the Upstash names set, the Worker skips the guard and logs the names once per isolate. Setting any of them requires a complete configuration, and the Worker refuses to serve otherwise. Compare the remaining Worker secrets with the Vercel project environment list before the flip.
- Optional variables read by the source: `MIND_APP_URL`, `WEB_APP_URL`.

## Mount activation known gaps

These are accepted for activation and fail closed; neither leaks a session.

- Logout fence loop (availability): with `__Host-tuturuuu_app_signed_out=1` on the apex, every mounted strict refresh answers `App signed out`. A page then goes to the mounted login, Web's login sees its valid session and returns to `/mind/verify-token`, whose fenced refresh sends it back to Web's login. Mind cannot clear the fence, because it writes no cookie on the apex and mounted app-only logout is refused there. Clearing it needs a Web-owned path.
- TOTP users cannot use the mount: strict mode refuses every user with a verified TOTP factor, at `aal1` or `aal2`: pages and APIs answer `403`, and `/mind/verify-token` sends them to Web's login with `mfa=required`. The production Worker redirects `mind.tuturuuu.com` to the mount, so after its cutover they cannot use Mind until the timestamp-aware verified-claims assurance contract is available to mounted sessions; before it, the Vercel deployment on `mind.tuturuuu.com` keeps serving them.

## Build and qualification

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun turbo:local run build --filter=@tuturuuu/mind^... --concurrency=2
bun scripts/ci/generate-build-metadata.ts
bun run --cwd apps/mind routes:check
bun run --cwd apps/mind type-check:cloudflare
bun run --cwd apps/mind build:cloudflare
CI=true CI_SOURCE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) bun run --cwd apps/mind test:runtime
```

`mind-cloudflare.yaml` runs the same steps in CI. `test:runtime` starts the emitted Worker in workerd
with synthetic secrets and no network egress: build identity, the root host (staging) or the
legacy-host `307`s with their open-redirect probes (production), apex rejection or the mount,
unknown paths, and the signed-out redirect through the app-owned
`cloudflare/auth-redirect.runtime.mjs` fixture (8 checks).

The app proxy admits anonymous `GET`/`HEAD /api/build-info` without an app-session
refresh, so deployment verification gets `200` instead of `401`.

## Smoke checks after the route is attached

```bash
curl -sI https://mind.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info   # 200, JSON, no-store
curl -sI 'https://mind.tuturuuu.com/boards?a=1'     # 307 to https://tuturuuu.com/mind/boards?a=1, private, no-store
curl -sI https://mind.tuturuuu.com/login            # 307 to https://tuturuuu.com/mind/login
curl -sI https://tuturuuu.com/mind                  # 307 to /mind/login for a signed-out client
```

Every page redirects signed-out users to login, so a signed-in check needs a test
session and belongs to the release owner. No smoke request may return `5xx`.

## Rollback

1. Before the flip, record the current production Vercel deployment id for the app (the repo
   does not store it) and the DNS records and TTLs for `mind.tuturuuu.com` in the release record.
2. Roll back by detaching the Worker route or restoring the captured DNS records to the
   recorded deployment. `vercel-production-mind.yaml` still deploys the Next app.
3. Rerun the smoke checks against the previous origin.

Rolling back touches no database rows and no migrations. Route, DNS and deployment
changes belong to the release owner.
